title: Preventing Initiative Fatigue
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece diagnoses 'initiative fatigue' not as a symptom of too many projects, but of too many things being treated as top priority simultaneously. It describes the arc from productivity high to exhaustion when leaders never signal which initiatives matter most. The recommended fix is explicit prioritization: giving a team a full list of initiatives but clearly naming which one matters most right now. The piece closes with a pointed self-check — if you can't name your top priorities on one hand, fatigue is already on its way.
points: Initiative fatigue is framed as a problem of too many priorities, not too many initiatives.
Teams pushed hard without clear priority signals move from pride in productivity to exhaustion.
Treating every initiative as equally urgent is identified as the core mistake leaders make.
The fix is explicit prioritization — naming which project matters most right now.
A simple self-check is offered: if you can't count your top priorities on one hand, fatigue is coming.
quotes: They can experience what is known as initiative fatigue, a weariness that robs them of their desire to perform.
Leaders who inadvertently burn out their teams generally do not have too many initiatives. They have too many priorities.
When leaders make every initiative a high priority, fatigue is soon to follow.
Fatigue and burnout are the result of too many priorities, not too many initiatives.
If you can’t count the most important initiatives on one hand, you’re setting the team up for fatigue and eventual failure.
